description: Narrative templates for FranchiseBook era chapters. Keyed by arc type + tense. Placeholders: {{teamName}}, {{teamCity}}, {{headCoach}}, {{startYear}}, {{endYear}}, {{wins}}, {{losses}}, {{winPct}}, {{titles}}, {{seasons}}, {{topPlayer}}.

openings: The {{teamName}} arrived in {{startYear}} not as favorites, but as believers.
Nothing about {{startYear}} foretold what the {{teamCity}} faithful were about to witness.
The climb began quietly in {{startYear}} — a few more wins, a few fewer collapses, a city daring to feel hopeful again.
In {{startYear}}, the {{teamName}} stopped losing and started meaning something.
signature: {{headCoach}} kept saying the same three words in press conferences: keep stacking bricks.
By the end, {{topPlayer}} had become the face of the rise — the player who refused to accept {{teamCity}}'s old ceiling.
The {{wins}}-{{losses}} record understates the shift in posture: the {{teamName}} no longer walked into stadiums expecting to lose.
Front-office trust deepened. The scouts were right more often than they were wrong.
closers: By {{endYear}}, the {{teamName}} were no longer the climb — they were the summit approach.
The ascent closed with {{titles}} parades still waiting, but the architecture was in place.
Chapter's end found {{teamCity}} believing again, and the league taking notes.

openings: This was the window. Everyone in {{teamCity}} knew it in {{startYear}}, and nobody wanted to waste it.
The {{teamName}} did not stumble into contention — they engineered it, brick by brick, under {{headCoach}}.
From {{startYear}} on, every Sunday in {{teamCity}} felt like the kind of Sunday a franchise is built around.
signature: {{topPlayer}} played like a man trying to pull a city onto his back, and often did.
The defense set the tone — disciplined, angry, unwilling to be outworked for four quarters.
Road crowds stopped laughing when the {{teamName}} came to town. That's how you know.
Internally, {{headCoach}} referred to this stretch as 'the ceiling we were always meant to hit.'
closers: The window closed, as windows do. But while it was open, {{teamCity}} had a real team — the kind you measure other eras by.
Peaks don't last. That's what makes them peaks. The {{teamName}} will spend the next era chasing this one.
{{wins}} wins, {{titles}} title-chase runs, one indelible era. The {{teamName}} had arrived.

openings: Every franchise gets a chance like this. Most waste it. The {{teamName}} did not.
Dynasties are built in the boring weeks — practices no one watches, meetings no one covers. The {{teamName}} of {{startYear}}–{{endYear}} lived there.
They will call this the golden era of {{teamCity}} football, and they will be right.
signature: Three words defined the stretch: standards, standards, standards. {{headCoach}} said it daily until the locker room lived it.
The {{teamName}} won {{titles}} titles — but what's remembered in {{teamCity}} is the expectation that came with every January.
{{topPlayer}} became the face, but the fingerprints are everywhere. This was a team.
Opponents didn't fear the {{teamName}} — they planned their entire years around them.
closers: By {{endYear}}, {{teamCity}} had become synonymous with winning, and every child wearing the colors believed it was supposed to be this way.
Eras end. Banners don't. The {{teamName}} raised {{titles}} and a generation's worth of memory.
The Golden Era closed the only way eras like this ever do — slowly, then suddenly — and {{teamCity}} was never quite the same.

openings: Nothing about {{startYear}}–{{endYear}} was easy in {{teamCity}}, and pretending otherwise would insult the fans who lived it.
The {{teamName}} spent this stretch in the wilderness, and the wilderness was unkind.
Every franchise has a valley. {{teamCity}}'s ran from {{startYear}} to {{endYear}}, and the fog rarely lifted.
signature: {{headCoach}} took the job knowing it was a rebuild, and the first wave of losses was still worse than advertised.
Injuries, bad luck, and deeper structural problems conspired. The front office had stopped being in denial by {{endYear}}, which was its own kind of progress.
{{topPlayer}} was often the only reason to show up — a single bright note in a long minor-key season.
Attendance dipped. Ownership pretended not to notice. The beat writers did.
closers: The valley was eventually survived, because all valleys are survived, but it left its mark on the roster and the city.
By {{endYear}}, the {{teamName}} had {{wins}} wins against {{losses}} losses — numbers that tell the story without embellishment.
The era closed with the team intact, the fanbase bruised, and a front office finally willing to tell the truth.

openings: A teardown is never announced — it's confessed. The {{teamName}} made theirs in {{startYear}}, and {{teamCity}} braced.
The {{teamName}} entered {{startYear}} with one honest sentence: we are not ready to contend.
Rebuilds work when the plan is longer than the patience. {{teamCity}}'s patience, to its credit, held.
signature: {{headCoach}} installed a culture first, a roster second. That was the bet.
Veterans were moved. Picks were stockpiled. The cap cleared. The playbook slimmed. The youth played.
Fans who had seen previous rebuilds fail waited — skeptical, exhausted, hopeful in rotation.
{{topPlayer}} was the hire of the era, brought in to anchor the next {{seasons}} seasons, not the current one.
closers: By {{endYear}}, the teardown had ended. What stood in its place was still unfinished — but it was finally scaffolding.
The rebuild closed quietly, which is the only way a good rebuild ever closes.
The {{wins}} wins across these years mattered less than the {{seasons}} that followed. That was the point.

openings: The {{teamName}} of {{startYear}}–{{endYear}} never settled. Never. That was the whole story.
Some eras find a rhythm. This one never did. {{teamCity}} rode every roller coaster the league could build.
From {{startYear}} on, the {{teamName}} were a different team every month.
signature: Twelve-win seasons followed five-win seasons followed twelve-win seasons. {{headCoach}} eventually stopped trying to explain it.
The locker room cycled through identities — tough, soft, veteran, young, again. Nothing held.
{{topPlayer}} was the one constant, even when the schemes around him weren't.
Fans learned to brace for everything and expect nothing. A survival skill.
closers: The era closed the way it had begun — unpredictably — and {{teamCity}} exhaled for no particular reason.
Turbulence eventually sorts itself into a pattern. By {{endYear}}, the {{teamName}} had one. Barely.
What this era lacked in consistency it made up for in incident. {{teamCity}} football was never boring.

openings: Not every era screams. The {{teamName}} of {{startYear}}–{{endYear}} were a hum — steady, competent, unshowy.
The {{teamName}} did not dominate or collapse between {{startYear}} and {{endYear}}. They competed, and they kept competing.
Mid-pack is not a crime. It is not a story. But it is a franchise's most common honest ground.
signature: {{headCoach}} ran a stable program. Nine wins most years. Wild Card most years. Nothing more, nothing less.
The {{teamName}} were the team nobody wanted to draw and nobody feared: a worthy opponent.
{{topPlayer}} did the job, every week. The roster was clean. The practices were clean. The cap was clean.
Ownership didn't fire anyone. The beat writers didn't have much to write. It was, in its way, a gift.
closers: The era closed with the {{teamName}} still intact, still respectable, still waiting for the leap.
{{wins}} wins, {{losses}} losses, {{titles}} titles. The ledger balanced. {{teamCity}} exhaled.
Steady eras do not make the highlight reels. They make the next era possible.

milestone_coda.three_peat_plus: Three titles in this window. Three. The {{teamName}} stopped being a team and became a standard.
milestone_coda.multi_title: Two rings in one era puts you in a very small club. The {{teamName}} found that club, and made room.
milestone_coda.first_title: The first one. After everything, the {{teamName}} finally had the first one.
milestone_coda.sustained_dominance: A {{winPct}} win rate across an era isn't luck. It's a system, a culture, and a refusal to waste a Sunday.
milestone_coda.deep_valley: There is no sugar-coating {{wins}}-{{losses}}. The franchise bottomed out, and the only honest path was up.
milestone_coda.dynasty_run: Future generations will argue about where this team ranks all-time. That is what the {{teamName}} earned.
milestone_coda.rollercoaster: Even the highlight reel needed two different soundtracks for this stretch. It never made sense, and it was never dull.
